faqs.question: What does the Fungal Stain test - Urine measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of fungal elements in your urine.

faqs.question: Why is the Fungal Stain test - Urine done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose fungal infections in the urinary tract • To monitor the effectiveness of antifungal treatment • To identify systemic fungal infections that can affect multiple organs • To guide appropriate therapy for patients with suspected fungal infections

faqs.question: When is the Fungal Stain test - Urine recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended if you have • symptoms suggesting a urinary tract infection caused by fungi, such as a burning sensation during urination or frequent urination, • a compromised immune system due to conditions like diabetes, HIV, or immunosuppressive therapy, or • suspected systemic fungal infection with symptoms such as fever, fatigue, or weight loss.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Fungal Stain test - Urine are abnormal?
faqs.answer: An abnormal result may indicate the presence of a fungal infection in the urinary tract or elsewhere in the body.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Fungal Stain test - Urine?
faqs.answer: During this test, you will have to provide a urine sample in a sterile container. The sample will be sent to the laboratory for analysis.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Fungal Stain test - Urine?
faqs.answer: • No fasting or other specific preparations are necessary for this test. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Fungal Stain test - Urine?
faqs.answer: • Urine culture: to identify the specific type of fungus causing the infection • Blood tests: to assess the presence of systemic fungal infections or monitor treatment response

faqs.question: What is the Fungal Stain by KOH & Calcofluor White Stain - Urine also known as?
faqs.answer: Urine Fungal Smear or KOH/Calcofluor White Stain - Urine

faqs.question: What is a fungal infection?
faqs.answer: A fungal infection is caused by the growth of fungi in or on the body. Fungi are common microorganisms found in the environment. Infections can occur in various parts of the body, including the skin, nails, respiratory tract, and urinary tract.
